name: Dawn

parts.name: Two solar arrays
parts.role: Huge dual solar array wings spanning nearly 20 meters tip-to-tip

parts.name: Core body
parts.role: Graphite composite core housing xenon propellant tanks

parts.name: Ion engine
parts.role: Three electrostatic xenon ion thrusters providing high specific impulse
parts.snap: Xenon ion thrusters glowing with gentle blue thrust.

parts.name: Dish antenna
parts.role: 1.52-meter high-gain parabolic antenna for communication across the asteroid belt

parts.name: Framing camera
parts.role: High-resolution optical framing camera for mapping craters and bright spots

parts.name: Sensors and trackers
parts.role: Star trackers and coarse Sun sensors for precision attitude determination
parts.snap: Star trackers locked onto celestial guides.

challenge.title: Point the antenna at Earth
challenge.intro: Hydrazine fuel is nearly depleted. Use short, precise thruster pulses to align the high-gain dish antenna with Earth's tracking beacon before signal fades.
challenge.hint: Tap Left and Right thruster burst buttons to null out angular drift and align inside the green Earth target cone.

signal_note: Dawn missed scheduled communications sessions on Oct 31 and Nov 1, 2018 after expending its last hydrazine fuel.
ending: Dawn was the first spacecraft to orbit two separate celestial bodies beyond the Earth-Moon system.
